lead.title: Inserm spinout EVerZom leads a €13.3M European consortium to test its extracellular vesicles in Crohn's disease fistulas, where Takeda failed
lead.deck: The five-year SATURN project brings together 12 partners in France, Spain, Germany, Italy and Belgium under the scientific leadership of Damián García-Olmo (Fundación Jiménez Díaz University Hospital, Madrid); EVerZom receives €2.7M to take EVerGel, vesicles derived from adipose-tissue mesenchymal stromal cells, injected around the perianal fistula with a temperature-sensitive hydrogel placed in the tract, into a Phase 1b/2a (29 to 38 patients, first patient targeted for October 2027) and then a Phase 2b (about 120 patients). Takeda withdrew its cell therapy Alofisel from the EU market in December 2024 after its Phase 3 failed (48.8% combined remission vs. 46.3% on placebo): the Paris-based biotech, which raised a €10M Series A in 2025 and now puts more than 80% of its resources into EVerGel, is betting on a more stable, standardized and re-dosable product.

milestone.title: Matisse Pharmaceuticals doses the first patient in SHIELDS-1, its Phase 2 trial of isupartob in sepsis
milestone.summary: Isupartob, a strongly negatively charged polyanion, captures the extracellular histones released by the immune system during sepsis, which damage blood vessels, fuel inflammation and drive organ failure. The randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, run in intensive care at eight Thai hospitals, first compares three dose regimens (80 patients) and then a single dose (140 patients), infused for up to 120 hours; interim results are expected by mid-2027.
milestone.why: Sepsis remains a graveyard for anti-inflammatory drugs: targeting one specific mediator of tissue damage, rather than the whole immune response, is a different bet. The Geleen company, funded by a Series A, secured FDA IND clearance and Fast Track designation in spring 2026: the mid-2027 interim readout will be its next catalyst.

deal.thesis: US-based Ritzey Therapeutics, launched with a $112.5M Series A led by Vida Ventures, is buying the Roscoff biotech founded in 2019 by Laurent Meijer, and with it leucettinib-21, an oral inhibitor of the DYRK1A kinase (encoded on chromosome 21) derived from a marine sponge compound, whose 152-participant Phase 1 finished in June 2026; Ritzey now plans Phase 2 studies of beta-cell function in type 1 and type 2 diabetes and in Down syndrome. A textbook case of a French academic asset, funded by some €6M in rounds and a €2.5M EIC grant, moving under a US flag right after Phase 1 to be repositioned toward a far broader indication than the original one.

brefsEurope.title: SERB and Hansa ask the EMA to convert Idefirix's conditional approval into a standard marketing authorization
brefsEurope.summary: The filing rests on the European post-authorization study of imlifidase, an enzyme that cleaves IgG antibodies to enable kidney transplantation in highly sensitized patients: 90% of patients met the primary endpoint of one-year graft failure-free survival (patient survival 98%, graft survival 92%). SERB has held the European license since July; in the US, the FDA's decision is due on December 19.

brefsEurope.title: Dicot Pharma wins French and Dutch clearance for the Phase 2b of LIB-01 in erectile dysfunction
brefsEurope.summary: Following Sweden, every participating country has now approved the study: at least 200 men across all severities, three monthly dose levels to select the Phase 3 dose, and a primary endpoint at week 12 on the IIEF-EF score. The first part, which sets the highest dose, has started in the US; European dosing will follow, expected in Q1 2027.

brefsEurope.title: Germany extends Staloral Birch and Staloral 3 Trees to children and adolescents aged 5 to 17
brefsEurope.summary: The Paul-Ehrlich-Institut broadened the label of these liquid sublingual immunotherapies on the strength of the Phase 3b YOBI trial: 553 young patients in 12 European countries, with a 41.7% improvement in the combined score vs. placebo in the second pollen season. A pediatric opening for allergen immunotherapy, the day after Desentum's positive Phase 2.

brefsEurope.title: The European Parliament adopts the pharmaceutical reform and the Critical Medicines Act
brefsEurope.summary: New medicines will get eight years of data protection plus one year of market protection, up to 11 years in total under conditions; priority antimicrobials can earn a one-year transferable exclusivity voucher. The Critical Medicines Act passed 592 to 35; most provisions will apply two years after publication in the Official Journal.

brefsEurope.title: Gabather doses the first patient in the TOTEMS Phase 2 of GT-002 for cognitive impairment in schizophrenia
brefsEurope.summary: GT-002, a partial positive allosteric modulator of the GABA-A receptor, is compared with oxazepam and placebo in a cross-over design in 20 patients and 30 healthy volunteers at the CNSR research center in Glostrup (Copenhagen University Hospital), funded by Innovation Fund Denmark. No drug is approved for these cognitive symptoms.

brefsEurope.title: In Science, the Max Planck team of Melina Schuh, Ovo Labs co-founder, stabilizes chromosomes in aging eggs
brefsEurope.summary: The engineered protein TALhesin binds near the center of chromosomes to hold sister chromatids together, standing in for cohesin that wears out with age: in older mice, the share of properly connected eggs rose from 47% to 74%. Ovo Labs has licensed the technology from Max Planck; it has not yet been tested in human eggs, while 50% to 80% of embryos from women over 40 carry chromosomal abnormalities.

brefsEurope.title: Latvia's Cellbox Labs secures up to €6.5M from the EIC Accelerator for its AI-driven organ-on-chip
brefsEurope.summary: A €2.5M grant and up to €4M in equity from the EIC Fund will fund microbiome-compatible human tissue models, automated experimentation (sensors, microscopy, environmental control) and an AI optimization loop. Targets: drug discovery and microbiome-based therapeutics.

brefsEurope.title: MicThera, a spinout of the Institute of Oncology Research in Bellinzona, raises a €4.75M seed for a prostate cancer biologic
brefsEurope.summary: The round, co-led by Indaco Venture Partners and LIFE BioCEEd with private investors, will take PV048, a first-in-class biologic active in treatment-resistant models, to clinical candidate nomination and IND-enabling studies. The Italian-Swiss company mines metagenomic data for its drug candidates.

brefsIntl.title: Medicare sets 2028 negotiated prices for 13 drugs, including Novartis' Cosentyx
brefsIntl.summary: In the third round under the Inflation Reduction Act, the agency estimates savings of $9.2B (45%) based on 2025 spending, or $5.5B once rebates are included; Trulicity, Orencia, Entyvio and Cimzia are also on the list, while Boehringer Ingelheim renegotiated Tradjenta. A benchmark for valuing European assets aimed at the US market.

word.definition: Membrane-bound nanoparticles, with no nucleus and unable to replicate, that cells naturally release to carry proteins, lipids and RNA to other cells: biotech uses them as a "cell-free" medicine or as a delivery vehicle.

parts.label: Producer cell
parts.role: often mesenchymal stromal cells, which give them their anti-inflammatory and reparative effect

parts.label: Lipid bilayer
parts.role: the envelope that protects the cargo and carries surface ligands

parts.label: Cargo
parts.role: proteins, mRNA and microRNA that reprogram the recipient cell

how.t: Cells are grown, often in bioreactors, and secrete vesicles into their culture medium.
Vesicles are separated and characterized (size, markers, purity) by ultrafiltration or chromatography, then quality-controlled batch by batch.
Once administered, they bind receptors or are taken up by target cells and release their cargo, which dampens inflammation and promotes repair.

word.why: They promise the effect of cell therapies without their risks (no proliferation or differentiation) and with the logistics of a drug: a storable, even freeze-dried, re-dosable product. The bottleneck is industrial: batch heterogeneity, non-standardized processes and poorly predictive potency assays, which the ISEV society's MISEV2023 guidelines aim to frame. Alofisel's failure at Takeda cooled the cell-based approach in Crohn's fistulas; EVerZom, backed by €13.3M in EU funding, is playing the vesicle version. A still underfunded field where Europe is ahead.

startups.name: EVerZom
startups.use: Inserm spinout: EVerGel, adipose stromal cell vesicles with a hydrogel, heading into a Phase 1b/2a in Crohn's fistulas (€13.3M SATURN EU consortium, November 2026)

startups.name: EXO Biologics
startups.use: EXOB-001, mesenchymal stem cell vesicles given via the endotracheal route to prevent bronchopulmonary dysplasia in extremely preterm infants; EVENEW Phase 1/2, the first EMA-authorized trial of this kind of exosome

startups.name: Ciloa
startups.use: CNRS and University of Montpellier spinout engineering exosomes to carry proteins; APN-sEV (adiponectin) candidate in type 2 diabetes and obesity, backed by €6.5M from France 2030 in 2025
